per_locus.title: Most users won't be able to claim their share of Uniswap fees
per_locus.evidence: F-001 names the exact mechanism: per-NFT fee accounting over a single shared Uniswap position with uninitialized feeGrowthInsideLast; first claimer collects all fees (pool.collect max) so most users cannot claim their share.

per_locus.title: Vultisig whitelisting can be bypassed by anyone
per_locus.evidence: F-006 identifies free unlimited self-whitelist via Whitelist.receive() (ETH refunded), i.e. anyone can whitelist themselves — the awarded 'whitelisting can be bypassed by anyone'.

per_locus.title: Adversary can prevent the launch of any ILO pool with enough raised capital at any moment by providing single-sided liquidity
per_locus.evidence: F-004 captures launch DoS via moving Uniswap slot0 away from initialPoolPriceX96 (require UV3P). Awarded uses single-sided liquidity to move the price; same mechanism (price nudge -> launch revert).

per_locus.title: Vultisig should be burnable
per_locus.evidence: Missing-feature finding (VULT token should implement burn). Not surfaced; no burn-capability analysis performed.

per_locus.title: `claim` function lacks slippage controls for `amount0` and `amount1` returned by `pool.burn` function call
per_locus.evidence: claim() was deeply analyzed (F-001 fee accounting, F-002 collect/transfer underflow) but the specific gap — pool.burn called with no amount0Min/amount1Min slippage control (MEV sandwich) — was not isolated.

per_locus.title: Transfer of `ILOPool` NFT token to different account allows for users to bypass the pool's `maxCapPerUser` invariant
per_locus.evidence: The per-user purchase-cap subsystem was examined and an adjacent cap-bypass finding (F-006, Whitelist maxAddressCap via Sybil) surfaced, but the ILOPool.buy maxCapPerUser bypass via transferring the position NFT (balanceOf->0 then re-buy) was not isolated.
